💷 £4.5 billion became £15.3 billion — and nobody lost their job over it.

The Home Office's asylum accommodation contracts were first estimated at £4.5bn in total. They're now forecast to cost £15.3bn over ten years. That's a £10.8bn gap on contracts the state wrote itself.

🏨 In 2024/25, hotels swallowed 76% of the annual cost — while housing just 35% of the people.

✅ To be straight with you: hotel numbers ARE falling — 30,657 at the end of 2025, down 19% on the year and 45% below the 2023 peak. Good. But emptying hotels and cutting the bill are not the same thing when the contract pays out either way.

⏰ There's a break clause in 2026. That's now. It's the one bit of leverage we have — and I'd bet good money it gets admired rather than used.

Full piece 👇
